newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha declines, shadows crude losses.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha declines, shadows crude losses.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices declined in quiet trade on Wednesday, following an overnight fall in crude prices, traders said.
"Although sentiment is relatively firm, naphtha prices may slip further as the crude market seems to be weakening," a trader said.

Open-spec naphtha first-half April was notionally assessed at $236.00/238.00, $1.00 below levels at the same time on Tuesday. First-half April switched hands at $238.00 in late Tuesday trade, traders said. Second-half April was assessed at $233.50/235.50, down from $234.50/236.00 on Tuesday.
Inter-month spreads remained stable with first-half April/first-half May at about $4.50/5.50.

In the physical market, about two Japanese end-users are believed to be seeking March cargoes, traders said. Market levels for March cargoes are about $6.00 to $7.00 above the mean of Singapore quotes, they said.
In the jet kerosene market, traders said a Japanese refiner bought a late February arrival cargo at about $32.70, on a c and f basis.
Low sulphur waxy residue traders said market activity was quiet, with Japanese interest remaining dull.(+81-5473-3708)
